sentences.text: 9. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the accused has contended that the deceased was suffering from T.B. and Asthama even prior to the marriage.
This aspect has been suppressed by PW-1 and her family members.

During the course of cross-examination of prosecution witnesses,
the illness of the deceased was suggested and it was also probabalized that the reason for the deceased to commit suicide was not on account of harassment, but it was because of the illness of the deceased.
The defence does not dispute the death of the deceased on account of hanging but probabalized its defence.
The evidence of PW-8 clearly explains that the accused and the deceased were leading cordial marital life.
The deceased was suffering from Asthama and Tuberculosis.
The evidence of PWs-2, 4, 5 cannot be relied as they never visited Belagavi till the incident.
There was no evidence to the effect that it was represented by PW-1 and her family members that the accused was a B.E. graduate and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.

Hence, the defence is more probable and also the evidence of the prosecution is unreliable, there are contradictions and omissions in the evidence and the evidence does not inspire the confidence of the Court.
For this reason, the trial court has not accepted the evidence and in view of the cloud of doubt, the benefit of doubt was extended to the accused and he has supported the impugned judgment.
10. We have perused the impugned judgment.
The trial court has recorded that the version of the prosecution that jewels and other articles have been given to the accused persons is not properly explained.
There are contradictions between the witnesses about the demand and payment of dowry.
The allegation of accused removing jewellery of the deceased is not properly explained.
The very marriage negotiations being participated by the women members of the Muslim community shows improvement in the case.
To create the evidence, the factum of illness of the deceased has been suppressed at the time of marriage.

There was no evidence to show that soon before the death,
the deceased was subjected to harassment in connection with demand of dowry.

The accused have produced evidence to show that by their business, they are earning huge amount in lakhs of money and paying the income-tax and there was any occasion for them to demand a meager sum of Rs.50,000/- as additional dowry.
Hence, demand of additional dowry is doubtful.
11. The trial court also recorded that in order to rebut the presumption under Section 113B of the Evidence Act, the prosecution has to discharge its initial burden, but it has not discharged it.

The Trial Court is very particular about the evidence of PWs-3 and 4 regarding payment of dowry, but their evidence did not point out clearly. CWs- 7, 9, 12, 16 to 24, 26 to 30, 32, 33, 38, 39, 40, 45 and 51 are shown as independent witnesses.
CWs-26, 30 and 32 are the neighbours residing in the same building where the accused and the deceased were residing.
But the prosecution did not examine these witnesses and there is no explanation for non-examination of material witnesses.

The trial court is very particular about the admission of PWs-1 and 8 in the cross-examination that they have noticed the cordial relationship between the deceased and the accused whenever they visited the house of the accused.
There was no complaint of harassment by the deceased.
There is no evidence regarding allegation of dowry demand from the very next day of the marriage.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Having heard the arguments advanced on both sides and also referring the weight of the evidence of the prosecution supra, the points that arise for our consideration are:
(i) Whether the prosecution evidence has satisfied the ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B and 306 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?
opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of the discussion made above,
we answer both the points raised above, in the negative.
The appeal deserves to be dismissed and the finding of the Trial Court is to be confirmed.
In the result, we pass the following;
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The judgment and order of acquittal dated 29.06.2016 passed in Sessions Case No.2/2010 on the file of the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi, at Belagavi, is hereby confirmed.
